user_request.summary: Build Phase 1 of a tiny-hero third-person 3D open-world room explorer with oversized furniture terrain, fixed-step parkour physics, pointer-lock camera, instanced clutter, adaptive rendering, warm indoor atmosphere, and a live parameter HUD in one HTML file.
goals: Create a 20m x 20m x 8m room perceived from a 0.1m-tall character scale.
Make the Giant Desk and Bookshelf Mountain traversable through reachable parkour steps and platforms.
Implement third-person momentum locomotion, jump, gravity, collision, and raycast ground/zone detection at 120Hz.
Use InstancedMesh for pencils, coins, paperclips, and bookshelf books.
Provide warm window lighting, soft shadows, dust motes, HUD telemetry, collectibles, and parameter authoring controls.
Maintain an adaptive near-native rendering ceiling with frustum/distance culling and visibility suspension.
requested_constraints: PointerLock API with standard mouse direction and drag fallback.
Fixed 120Hz internal physics with normal requestAnimationFrame rendering.
Real-time controls for jump force, move speed, camera sensitivity, and dust density.

reversible_assumptions: Desktop keyboard and mouse are the primary Phase 1 input surface.
The player collision body is an upright capsule approximation represented by an AABB plus downward raycast.
Furniture collision is axis-aligned except for non-collidable decorative meshes.
The room uses a deliberately compressed parkour route so a 0.1m hero can reach desk and shelf elevations without unrealistic global jump scaling.

derived_constraints.name: Embedded Three.js runtime
derived_constraints.reason: The deliverable must execute as one HTML file even when local-file CDN/module access is blocked.
derived_constraints.benefit: The authored HTML opens directly from disk with zero network requests, no local server, and no package installation.
derived_constraints.rejected_alternative: Pinned CDN mirrors were rejected after a real offline launch failure; a custom partial 3D engine would reduce lighting, shadow, instancing, culling, and raycast quality.
derived_constraints.visual_cost: The HTML is approximately 760 KB because the renderer is bundled inline.

derived_constraints.name: No general rigid-body engine
derived_constraints.reason: Phase 1 traversal needs deterministic character/platform collision rather than arbitrary object dynamics.
derived_constraints.benefit: Small fixed-step state, predictable 120Hz behavior, and low CPU overhead.
derived_constraints.rejected_alternative: Bundling a second physics dependency would violate the lean single-file objective and add unnecessary simulation cost.
derived_constraints.visual_cost: Furniture and scatter props are static; pushing and stacking are deferred.

considered: Warm afternoon bedroom expedition with sunlit dust and toy-like materials
Night-time desk city with emissive electronics

concepts.selected: Warm afternoon bedroom expedition with furniture-as-skyscrapers
concepts.selection_rationale: It best communicates tiny scale through familiar materials, long shadows, visible dust, floor-level parallax, and bright navigational landmarks.

representation.stack: Embedded Three.js r179 WebGLRenderer + procedural geometry + DOM authoring HUD
representation.ceiling_rationale: The world depends on real scale, depth, surface contact, inspectable geometry, and vertical traversal; a 2D representation cannot satisfy the capability problem.

system.source_of_truth: Deterministic PlayerState and parameter store advanced at a fixed 1/120 second step.
